description: Test-command allowlist per framework (DEPT28_SPEC D7, SP-03). argv only, no shell; the engine runs these (RED, GREEN, revert check, suite), never the agent's own command. {target} is the single test target <path>::<name> relative to the service directory, expanded per ecosystem by engine/toolchains.py (pytest: the node id; go: -run '^Name$' ./dir; cargo: --test <bin>|--lib|--bin <name> -- <name> --exact; node: --test-name-pattern='^name$' <file>); the suite form has no target. Framework detection is by marker file inside services/<service>/. Round 18 R2 for EVERY framework: the engine appends its OWN options (pytest: -c <engine ini> with addopts empty, --rootdir, -o overrides from 'ini', --junitxml to an engine path; cargo: --target-dir under the engine directory; node: --test-reporter=junit to an engine path plus the TAP reporter on stdout; go: the seeded -json stream) and reads the verdict from the engine-owned artefact cross-checked against 'collect' (pytest --collect-only, go test -json -list, cargo test -- --list; node has none, stated), the transcript and the exit code. The repository's own test configuration is never read. 'test_infra_globs' name the files an agent may not change in an engine run (R1: any change fails the round with test_infra_changed); 'test_content_deny' are regexes a changed or new TEST file may not match (the cheap forgery routes of that ecosystem's transcript; a hit fails the round test_content_denied). 'target_example' is the example target shown in the brief. Hash pinned in config.py. Round 19 R1: every engine run happens in a FRESH container from an engine-built tree; 'src_content_deny' are regexes a changed SOURCE file may not match (a hit fails the round src_content_denied).

pytest.note: detected by a Python project file, never by a bare tests/ directory (every ecosystem has one). Round 19 R4: pytest runs with --disable-plugin-autoload and -p zbm_engine_plugin (the engine's own plugin, first on pythonpath; a tree entry named zbm_engine_plugin* is test infra); test_content_deny refuses the cheap re-plugging spellings in a test file and src_content_deny the same in a changed source file (stated as cheap layers). Wave 21 (N20-D-8): test_content_deny also refuses, as the same cheap layer (a regex over the test file's text, not a proof), a test that exits the process (os._exit, sys.exit, SystemExit, pytest.exit, os.abort/kill, exit()/quit()), writes at the fd level (os.write/dup/dup2/fdopen, sys.__stdout__/__stderr__, /dev/stdout|stderr|tty|fd, /proc/self/fd, open(1|2), .fileno()) or bypasses pytest's capture (capsys/capfd, .disabled(), the terminal reporter) - the routes to the runner's transcript the engine note names; the verdict still comes from the engine's junit file and its own plugin record. Wave 22 (G1, N21-D-1): src_content_deny is the CHEAP layer of runner-detection refusals, applied to the lines a fix ADDS to a source file (a new source file: all of it): test-runner name literals, sys.modules lookups of test frameworks, PYTEST_ names, os.environ/getenv reads of CI/PYTEST*/TEST*, unittest.mock, frame/stack introspection, /proc/self/environ|cmdline and sys.flags. A regex over text, not a proof: the STRUCTURAL layer is the engine's runner-independent re-execution of the finding's reproduction outside pytest (adapters/tools/zbm_standalone_runner.py; python -I, pytest not importable, CI/PYTEST*/TEST* scrubbed), which must pass with the fix and fail on the reverted checkout before candidate_passed_checks. Wave 24 (E4, N23-D-3): test_framework_import refuses a source line that imports pytest, _pytest or unittest (production never needs them; the standalone run's import hook blames such an import on the source).

cargo.note: stable toolchain only: -Z unstable-options --format json (nightly) is not used and cargo nextest is not a dependency of this build (ADR 0011). The RED test must be a separate test file under tests/ (an integration test): a #[cfg(test)] unit test inside a source file cannot be split from the source by the R1 verification checkouts. Every test binary of the package runs (--no-fail-fast); a workspace is run from its root. Wave 22 (G1): src_content_deny refuses RUST_TEST*, cfg!(test), the libtest arguments, CI/TEST/CARGO_* env reads and backtrace capture in the lines a fix adds to a source file; the reproduction is also re-run with the CI markers unset. The same libtest harness runs both (residual, ADR 0011).

go.note: -race and -count=1 per the repository's CI; -json is test2json-framed so a test's own prints are output events, never results; the listing is go test -json -list per package (Test* functions only: examples and benchmarks are not counted). Sub-tests are recorded but the count is per top-level Test function. Wave 22 (G1): src_content_deny refuses the cheap runner-detection spellings in the lines a fix adds to a non-test .go file (testing.Testing(), -test.* flags, the testing import, CI/TEST env reads, runtime.Caller*/debug.Stack); the finding's reproduction is also re-run with CI and the CI markers unset (env -u) and must pass with the fix and fail reverted. The same go test runs both: a check of the test binary itself is only the cheap layer (residual, ADR 0011).

npm.note: only with a lockfile present (D7); no npm install is ever run by the engine and node_modules is never shipped to a verification checkout, so a test must run on Node's built-ins and the service's own sources. Node 22 has no collect-only mechanism: the junit report is cross-checked against the TAP stream and the exit code (stated in ADR 0011). A test's name must be an identifier (the TEST: grammar), matched with --test-name-pattern='^name$'. Wave 22 (G1): src_content_deny refuses NODE_TEST_CONTEXT, node:test, --test argv checks, NODE_ENV === 'test', CI/TEST env reads and stack capture in the lines a fix adds to a source file; the reproduction is also re-run with the CI markers unset. node --test sets NODE_TEST_CONTEXT for the test process itself, which env -u cannot remove (residual, ADR 0011).
